findings.detail: This question has the same problem as the earlier question M3-S36-T1. Both questions show an Agent SDK tool refining an automation script. In both, a test run reports two interacting problems and one independent wording problem: date parser plus file naming plus help text typo, against branch age plus protected-branch filter plus log message wording. Both have the same correct action: report the interacting problems together in one detailed message and handle the independent problem in its own iteration. Options C and E only split that earlier correct option into two rules. The wrong options change, but the reasoning that leads to the answer is the same. A new question on 3.5-K4 needs a different problem. Examples: a case where all the problems are independent, so sequential iteration is correct; or diagnosing why sequential fixes kept breaking each other.

blind_answer.reason: Per 3.5-K4/S5, fixes that interact should go together in one detailed message (C), and independent problems can be fixed one at a time in sequential iterations (E). What decides it is whether the fixes interact, not file location, list length, or severity.
